title: Sub-Scope Report Customisation Architecture
summary: define the docs_subscope default, registered collection customisations, toolbar ownership, public isolation, and lifecycle integration
content_html:
Sub-Scope Report Customisation Architecture

Architecture Outcome

Every configured one-level sub-scope uses the same docs_subscope engine and one useful default. A sub-scope may select a registered customisation module when its own content or workflow needs more than that default.

configured collection
  -> docs_subscope engine
  -> default presentation and Manage actions
  -> optional registered collection customisation

The customisation is an explicit property of the collection, not an inferred variant of viewer_report, a filename convention, or a condition on a known scope or sub-scope ID.

Collection And Host Identity

The collection remains {scope, sub_scope}. Child documents remain exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} targets.

The indexed host is an ordinary parent-scope document containing:

viewer_report: docs_subscope
viewer_report_access: local
viewer_report_subscope: <sub-scope-id>

The host selects the engine and collection only. The configured sub-scope record selects a known customisation identity; absence means the default. Config must never contain an arbitrary JavaScript module path.

Definition Of The Default

The default is the complete minimum useful report for an ordinary flat document collection. It is not Analysis/Tags with optional labels removed.

Shared public-safe behaviour:

  • collection validation and ordered membership;
  • list, detail, empty, unavailable, and error states;
  • title search over the loaded collection;
  • validated by-ID loading and subdoc navigation; and
  • clean absence of management controls.

Default Manage behaviour adds:

  • the accepted compact management row presentation;
  • exact-collection New document, including for an empty collection; and
  • capability-aware omitted or disabled states without target fallback.

Filters beyond title search, selection workflows, package actions, additional row fields, and collection-specific detail actions are not automatically part of the default.

The public manifest remains compact {doc_id, title} data. The Manage manifest remains a data projection, not an action registry. Its required default fields and any visible use of last_updated are frozen by the first delivery. An unused field is not added merely because it is available in source front matter.

Isolated Candidate And Cutover

SSR-1 develops the default through an explicitly temporary local-only report identity, provisionally docs_subscope_candidate.

The candidate copies the current shared report module so work on its structure cannot regress the canonical docs_subscope used by Analysis/Tags. Copying the report module alone is insufficient: the Manage host currently gives every docs_subscope the same contribution containing New, selection, Prepare Package, Delete, row state, and Import-context publication. The candidate must therefore receive its own minimal default Manage composition as well.

The isolation boundary is narrow:

  • copy the shared report module that is being reworked;
  • add a local-only loader and explicit temporary Manage dispatch;
  • create a new minimal default Manage contribution rather than changing the existing Tags-shaped contribution in place;
  • reuse generic filter, URL, target, action, selection, and lifecycle helpers where their contracts already fit; and
  • reuse the one sub-scope builder and its public/Manage manifest generation.

The candidate is not added to the public report loader. Its Studio host uses the temporary report ID only while SSR-1 is active; final host front matter uses canonical viewer_report: docs_subscope.

Cutover occurs only after the studio/default empty/list/detail/action surface is accepted and Analysis/Tags passes parity through its registered customisation. In the same delivery:

  1. canonical docs_subscope resolves the accepted implementation;
  2. the Studio fixture host switches to canonical docs_subscope;
  3. Analysis/Tags switches to canonical default plus its customisation; and
  4. the candidate report registry row, loader entry, temporary Manage dispatch, and superseded module/contribution wiring are removed.

There is no permanent alias and no runtime condition on sub_scope: default.

Customisation Resolution

A controlled registry maps each known customisation identity to its allowed contributions:

sub-scope config identity
  -> safe registry entry
  -> shared/public contribution, when one exists
  -> Manage contribution, when capability and access allow it

Unknown identities fail as configuration errors. Public routes cannot import Manage modules, local capability data, or mutation workflows.

A collection customisation may compose reusable feature helpers, but it owns the decision to include them. The standard contribution contract must cover:

  • row or row-metadata presentation;
  • controls adjacent to default title search;
  • list-toolbar controls;
  • collection-local selection controls and actions;
  • validated-detail controls; and
  • mount, state, refresh, and unmount lifecycle events.

Every rendered action declares a stable identity, placement, target kind, capability requirement, empty-state behaviour, handler owner, and refresh effect. Actions consume only their explicit collection, checked IDs, or validated document target.

Toolbar Ownership

The default Manage contribution owns New document because creating the first child is basic collection behaviour.

An optional customisation owns the composition of its additional controls. It may reuse common selection, package, Delete, status, or filtering helpers, but those helpers do not activate themselves based on manifest shape or a known collection ID.

The single app-level Import action remains outside the report toolbar. A mounted report may publish its exact collection and refresh callbacks through the standard lifecycle seam; it does not create another Import button.

Analysis/Tags Retrofit

Analysis/Tags becomes one registered customisation of the default report.

The default continues to provide title search, list/detail navigation, and New. The Analysis/Tags module owns the additional composition required for:

  • configured group filtering and group order;
  • status and non-viewable row treatment if these are not accepted as default;
  • collection-local selection and Prepare Package;
  • validated-detail Delete; and
  • collection/refresh publication needed by app-level Import.

Manage title Tags and public title Concepts remain resolved collection configuration, not a new report type. No analysis, tags, concept, or known group value belongs in the default engine or customisation dispatcher.

The refactor removes superseded direct wiring after parity is proven. It does not retain a hidden legacy Tags route alongside the registered module.

Lifecycle Integration

The New sub-scope lifecycle creates a collection with no customisation identity. It also creates one associated parent report host and valid empty public-safe and Manage projections, then refreshes configuration and parent discovery before navigating to the exact returned host.

The association between lifecycle-created collection and host is explicit and stable. Later deletion previews and applies against that exact association; it must not infer the host from title, filename, active document, or URL text.

Post-commit refresh or navigation failure returns the committed identities and retries follow-through only. It never creates another collection or host.

Projects Decision Boundary

The dotlineform/projects collection first receives the default through the normal lifecycle. Its real documents and management workflow are then reviewed before any Projects module is designed.

Possible differences—metadata, grouping, status, sorting, filters, or actions—are evidence prompts, not assumed requirements. The decision may be that the default is sufficient. If customisation is justified, Projects uses the same config identity, registry, contribution positions, exact targets, and public/Manage boundary as Analysis/Tags.

Decisions Owned By Delivery

The first delivery freezes:

  • the exact sub-scope config field and registry shape;
  • the default Manage row fields and whether last_updated has a visible use;
  • which current row/status helpers are default versus optional;
  • contribution placement and lifecycle payloads; and
  • the final module ownership and filenames after current-code inspection.

The second delivery freezes the lifecycle association and failure shape. The third decides only the Projects-specific needs that can be justified from the working default.

The feature parent owns delivery order and status.
